chunks: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about an umm walad belonging to a man, whom he had sent for hajj. Would that suffice for her as the Hajj of Islam? He said: "No." I said: "Is there a reward for her in her hajj?" He said: "Yes."

key_terms.أَجْرٌ: reward from Allah for the act
key_terms.أَحَجَّهَا: he sent her to perform hajj
key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: a slave-concubine who has borne her master a child
key_terms.حَجَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required in Islam

ai.seo_question: Does a slave woman’s hajj count as her obligatory Hajj of Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if an umm walad is sent for hajj by her master, that hajj does not fulfill her obligatory Hajj of Islam. However, she still receives reward for performing it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (as) about a concubine (umm walad) of a man whom he had sent for Hajj. "Does that suffice for her as the Hajj of Islam?"
Imam (as) said: "No."
I asked: "Does she have any reward for her Hajj?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes."
